SMTO-SKL-0188 — This file is too large for SMTO's GitHub transfer

GUID: edb4099c-a58d-5ffd-aeae-bfa28eb108f6
Slug: github-file-too-large
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO can send or receive files of up to 100 MB with GitHub, and this one is bigger, so SMTO stopped. No partial file was saved or uploaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. For an upload, make the file smaller, such as compressing it into a zip or splitting it into parts under 100 MB, then attach the smaller file to this Conversation. SMTO never splits or shrinks files for you, so the file itself must fit the limit.
  2. Ask the Agent to upload the smaller file or files. Nothing was uploaded this time, so trying again with a file under the limit is safe.
  3. For a download over 100 MB, or a file you can't shrink, download or upload it directly on github.com in your web browser instead. The 100 MB limit is built into SMTO's GitHub tools and can't be changed in Settings.

What success looks like

  • The Agent confirms the transfer and the file appears on GitHub or in the Conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the file's size.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A GitHub file transfer exceeded the 100 MiB limit: either the upload source artifact is larger than 100 MiB or the streamed download passed 100 MiB, so the transfer was stopped and no partial file was saved.

What this means

  • Upload source or streamed download exceeds 100 MiB. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Upload source or streamed download exceeds 100 MiB.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare actual byte count with the 100 MiB bound.

How to fix it

  • Use a source or target of at most 100 MiB (MAX_FILE_BYTES). The skill does not split, compress or inline large assets; compress or split the file yourself, or transfer it outside SMTO (for example GitHub's web UI or gh CLI). For downloads, choose a smaller artifact or log.
  • Select a file of at most 100 MiB. This skill does not inline or split large assets automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberately selected file within the supported bound completes the transfer.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
